headline: A new census found that of 1,357 FDA-cleared AI medical devices, only three have been tested on whether patients actually do better.
score_reason: Strong evidence-gap finding, but public-records only and no non-AI comparison.
importance_line: Patients and hospitals relying on cleared AI tools may not know if they improve outcomes, but the authors stress that untested does not mean unsafe and unregistered studies would be missed.
summary: Earth.com reports that a census by researchers at the University of Toronto and MIT Critical Data, published in PLOS Digital Health, found that only 34 of 1,357 FDA-cleared AI devices have a registered trial and just three were studied for patient outcomes. Most devices reached the market through the 510(k) route, which requires similarity to an existing device rather than a new trial; the authors note that unregistered company studies would not appear in their count.
notes: Data cutoff 5 Dec 2025 stated in article.
